summaryHeading: A traffic warrant in El Paso can be recalled without an arrest
summary: When you miss the appearance date on a citation, El Paso Municipal Court and the area courts issue a warrant on the ticket and generally file a separate failure-to-appear charge beside it.
A hired attorney can ask the court to recall a Class C traffic warrant without you being arrested or posting a cash bond. We file the paperwork; the court resets the case to a regular docket.

Our warrant fee is $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional warrant, on top of the flat $59–$69 ticket fee. Timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised.
Not sure whether you have a warrant? Use our free ticket and warrant lookup and we will check the El Paso County courts for you.

sections.heading: How a Missed Appearance Date Becomes a Warrant
paragraphs: Every citation in El Paso carries an appearance date, commonly a few weeks after the stop. If nothing happens by that date — no payment, no plea, no attorney on file — the court treats the silence as a failure to appear. El Paso Municipal Court then issues an arrest warrant on the original ticket and, in the typical case, files a second Class C charge for violating the promise to appear. One ticket becomes two cases and a warrant.
The same process runs in the Justice of the Peace precincts and the area city courts, and each keeps its own warrant list.

A warrant does not expire with time. It stays active until the case is resolved, and the court can also report the unresolved case to the Texas Department of Public Safety, which leads to an OMNI hold on your driver's license renewal.

sections.heading: Three Ways a Warrant Comes Off the List — and What Each One Costs You
paragraphs: People use "recall" and "lift" interchangeably; both mean the judge withdraws the warrant so officers no longer have authority to arrest you on it. What differs is how it gets withdrawn, because the three routes cost very different amounts of money and stress.

You can post a cash bond on every case, which often means several hundred dollars up front just to get a new court date. You can wait to be arrested and booked at the county jail. Or you can hire an attorney to file an appearance and a request to recall — with an attorney bond where the court requires one — so the court resets the case without a cash bond or a trip to the jail.

On top of that, the warrant work is $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional warrant. A driver with one ticket and one warrant in Municipal Court pays $94 to have the warrant recalled and the ticket defended, with no bondsman involved.

Once you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file the notice of appearance and the request to recall. Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised. We confirm with the clerk that the warrant is out of the system before we tell you it is clear.

From that point the case is an open ticket on a pretrial docket, and we handle it like any other citation: our goal is to pursue the best available outcome based on the citation, driving record, court and circumstances — commonly a dismissal or deferred disposition so the original violation does not become a conviction. For a Class C ticket, you generally do not have to appear.

sections.heading: Where Old Warrants Surface: Roundups, Traffic Stops and the DPS Counter
paragraphs: Texas courts, El Paso Municipal Court among them, have periodically taken part in a statewide warrant roundup, usually announced in advance with a short window to resolve cases before officers begin serving Class C warrants at homes and workplaces. If you have an old ticket warrant, the weeks before any announced roundup are the time to deal with it on your own terms.

The rest of the year, the most common way a warrant surfaces is an ordinary traffic stop. An officer on Mesa Street or Loop 375 runs your license, the warrant appears, and a routine stop for a speeding ticket ends with handcuffs and a tow. Warrants also surface when you try to renew your license and discover the OMNI hold.

It is cheaper and far less disruptive to recall a warrant on your schedule than on the officer's. Our traffic warrants overview explains how the warrant, the second charge and the license hold fit together.

sections.heading: Warrants in JP, Horizon City, Socorro and the Valley Courts
paragraphs: We handle traffic warrants in the courts across El Paso County: El Paso Municipal Court, the Justice of the Peace precincts, and the Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint, Anthony and Vinton municipal courts. Fort Bliss soldiers and clients who have moved out of state are a real share of this work, because an attorney appearance means no trip back for a Class C case.

Because each court keeps its own list, the first step is the same every time: find every warrant. Our free lookup form takes your name and date of birth, and our office checks each court and reports back what is open, where it is, and the fee to clear it. Se habla español.

sections.heading: What to Do Today, and What to Send Us
paragraphs: Do not drive to the courthouse to "ask" — if the warrant is active, you can be arrested at the window. Do not pay the ticket online either: paying enters a plea and a conviction on your DPS record, and it may not close the separate failure-to-appear case. Fill out the lookup form or call us, and let us file the recall.

faqs.q: How fast can you get a traffic warrant lifted in El Paso?
faqs.a: Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised. Smaller courts like Horizon City and Socorro act on the days their judge sits. We confirm directly with the clerk before telling you the warrant is clear.

faqs.q: Will I have to go to jail or see a bondsman?
faqs.a: Generally not for a Class C traffic warrant. An attorney appearance lets the court recall the warrant without an arrest, a cash bond from you, or a bail bondsman. You stay home, we file the paperwork, and the court resets your case to a normal docket.

faqs.q: What does a warrant recall cost?
faqs.a: The warrant work is $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional warrant. That is added to the flat ticket fee of $59 in El Paso Municipal Court or $69 in JP and the smaller city courts. Court fines and costs, if any, are set by the court and depend on how the case resolves.

faqs.q: Does recalling the warrant make the ticket go away?
faqs.a: No. It reopens the ticket so it can be defended. After the recall we handle the original citation and the failure-to-appear charge together, working toward a dismissal or deferred disposition where the court allows it. See our failure to appear page for how both cases resolve.

faqs.q: I moved away from El Paso. Can you still clear my warrant?
faqs.a: Yes. We represent clients who now live elsewhere in Texas, out of state and overseas. Because our office appears for you, you generally do not need to travel back to El Paso for a Class C traffic warrant.

faqs.q: How do I find out if I have a warrant in El Paso?
faqs.a: Use our free ticket and warrant lookup. We check El Paso Municipal Court, the JP precincts and the area city courts and tell you what is outstanding, where, and what it will cost to clear.
